blocks.text: 1. Multi-Modal RAG

blocks.alt: Text, image, and table all feed a shared index

blocks.text: Knowledge Graph RAG closed by weighing when its construction cost is worth it. Multi-Modal RAG, retrieval across text, images, and other content types together, closes out the entire Advanced RAG module by relaxing the text-only assumption every earlier pattern made.
It embeds different content types into a shared space so they can be retrieved side by side.
2. Beyond Text-Only Documents

blocks.alt: Text only is compared against text, images, and tables

blocks.text: Every pattern covered so far in this module assumed the source content was plain text.
Real knowledge bases also contain images, tables, and diagrams worth retrieving too.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Content type","Handled by text-only retrieval"],"rows":[["Plain text chunks","Yes, the default case for every earlier pattern"],["Images, tables, diagrams","No requires multi-modal retrieval instead"]]}

blocks.text: 3. A Shared Embedding Space Across Modalities

blocks.alt: A text embedding and image embedding share the same space

blocks.text: A multi-modal embedding model maps text and images into the same vector space.
Allowing a text query to retrieve a relevant image directly by similarity.
4. Retrieving Across Mixed Content Types

blocks.alt: A query produces both text and image results

blocks.text: A single query can retrieve a mix of matching text chunks and matching images in one ranked result set.
Rather than running separate, disconnected searches per content type.
5. Presenting Mixed Content To The Generator

blocks.alt: A text chunk and image chunk are both passed to the generator

blocks.text: In Prompt Engineering for RAG, the generation model itself must be able to accept both text and image input together.
Not every generation model supports that combined input.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A retrieved image passed to a text-only generation model, cannot be used at all, since the model has no way to accept image input regardless of how well it was retrieved.
blocks.text: A retrieved image passed to a text-only generation model cannot be used at all, since the model has no way to accept image input regardless of how well it was retrieved.
6. Extracting Text From Images And Tables

blocks.alt: An image or table goes through OCR or extraction to produce extracted text

blocks.text: As with metadata extraction in Document Ingestion, a simpler fallback extracts a text description or table structure from an image at ingestion time.
Then retrieves that extracted text like any other chunk.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Approach","What the model actually sees"],"rows":[["Text extraction fallback","A text description generated from the image"],["True multi-modal retrieval","The original image itself"]]}

blocks.text: 7. True Multi-Modal Versus Text Fallback
True multi-modal retrieval preserves the original image for the model to see directly.
While the text extraction fallback loses whatever the description failed to capture.
8. Multi-Modal Pipelines Need More Infrastructure
As with each added step costs latency in Advanced RAG, storing and indexing multiple content types requires more infrastructure than a text-only vector index.
A real cost beyond the embedding model choice alone.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: Storing raw images alongside their embeddings, adds real storage and indexing infrastructure beyond what a text-only vector database needs, a cost worth weighing before committing to true multi-modal retrieval.
blocks.text: Storing raw images alongside their embeddings adds real storage and indexing infrastructure beyond what a text-only vector database needs, a cost worth weighing before committing to true multi-modal retrieval.
9. Recognizing When Multi-Modal RAG Earns Its Added Infrastructure

blocks.alt: Documents containing images or tables points toward multi-modal RAG

blocks.text: A knowledge base rich in diagrams, charts, or images benefits from multi-modal retrieval.
A knowledge base that is entirely plain text never needs the added modality support.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Assuming a text-only generation model can accept a retrieved image without checking first.
Relying only on a text extraction fallback when the original image detail actually matters.
Underestimating the storage and indexing infrastructure multi-modal retrieval requires.
Building multi-modal retrieval for a knowledge base that is entirely plain text.

blocks.text: 12. Advanced RAG: Module Complete

items: Naive RAG: the simplest four stage retrieve then generate pipeline, and this module's baseline.
Advanced RAG: the general shift toward pre-retrieval and post-retrieval correction stages.
Modular RAG: treating each pipeline stage as a swappable, independent module.
Corrective RAG (CRAG): grading retrieved chunks and correcting a poor retrieval with a fallback.
Self-RAG: a model trained to reflect on its own retrieval and generation decisions inline.
Adaptive RAG: classifying query complexity first, then routing to a matching strategy.
Fusion RAG: combining results from multiple retrieval passes with reciprocal rank fusion.
Graph RAG: retrieving by traversing relationships between entities in a knowledge graph.
Agentic RAG: an autonomous agent choosing tools and deciding when enough information exists.
Recursive RAG: repeatedly refining retrieval results across bounded rounds.
Multi-Hop RAG: chasing a chain of dependent facts across several retrieval steps.
Knowledge Graph RAG: retrieval grounded entirely in a pre-built, schema-driven structured graph.
Multi-Modal RAG: retrieving text, images, and other content types together from a shared space.
This closes the Advanced RAG module; the Agentic RAG module covers autonomous agent patterns in much greater depth next.
